transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep snapping at people. Like at work, we had this safety meeting and I started yelling before I could even stop myself. Now the younger inspectors seem scared to ask me anything. I don’t want to be like that.
Do you find yourself getting angry or irritable in situations outside of work, like at home or in social settings?

Yes. It’s not just work. I get irritated fast with people, and sometimes I snap before I’ve even had a chance to think. Then afterward I feel bad because I can see they’re kind of walking on eggshells around me.
How often do these feelings of irritability and anger come up for you—do they happen almost every day, or are there days when you feel more like yourself?

It feels like it’s most days lately. I mean, not every minute of the day, but it comes up a lot. I’ll be okay and then something small happens, and I’m snapping before I even really think about it. That safety meeting was a bad one—I started yelling, and now some of the younger inspectors seem scared to even ask me things.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought of it that way. I know I’ve been on edge and short with people, but as far as feeling hopeless or not caring about things… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, even a little bit?

I don’t really know. I mean, I haven’t been paying attention to whether I’m sad or not enjoying things. I mostly just notice that I’m tense and short with people. As far as losing interest, I’m not sure.
Over the past few weeks, have you had days where you felt down or sad most of the time, even when things weren’t particularly stressful?

I’m not sure. I can’t really say I’ve had whole days where I felt sad most of the time. I haven’t been tracking it like that. I mostly notice when I’m stressed or tense, but the sad part… I don’t know.
Have you noticed any days where you felt down or lost interest in things, even for a short while, over the past few weeks?
I really can’t say. I haven’t noticed that in any clear way, even for a short while. I’ve just not been paying attention to it like that.
Have you experienced any days in the past month where you felt little pleasure or joy in things you usually like doing, even for a short time?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it that way, like feeling no joy in things. I guess I just haven’t been paying close attention to that.
Have you noticed that your mood feels irritable or tense even when you’re not in a stressful situation or around other people?

Yes. I stay tense a lot, and I get irritable fast. That’s part of why I’m here — I keep snapping at people. At a safety meeting I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now some of the younger inspectors seem scared to even ask me anything.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, or feeling tired even when you haven’t been physically active?

Yes. Even when I’m just in the break room or at rehearsal, I can’t settle. I’m watching the doors, listening for sudden machine noises, checking if somebody’s moving behind me. It’s like my body won’t believe I’m safe, even when nothing is happening.
Do you find yourself being very watchful or easily startled, even in situations where there’s no real danger?

Yes. I’m on alert even when there’s no reason to be. Like in the break room or at rehearsal, I’m watching the doors, listening for sudden machine noises, checking who’s moving behind me. It’s like my body just won’t accept that I’m safe.
Do you often feel like you're on high alert, even in places where you should feel safe, like at home or with friends?

Yes. Even places that should feel normal don’t feel that way. In the break room or at rehearsal, I’m watching the doors, listening for sudden machine noises, checking if somebody’s moving behind me. I know there’s probably no real danger, but my body just won’t believe I’m safe.
Have you had any experiences where you feel like you're reliving a stressful or traumatic event, like a memory popping into your mind when you don't expect it?

Yes. It happens out of nowhere. A clank from a cart, or even the smell of hot oil, and suddenly I’m right back in that bay. I can see my coworker by the machine like it’s happening in front of me all over again.
Have you noticed yourself feeling detached or distant from other people, or have you lost interest in things that used to matter to you, even for a short time?

I’m not really sure. I don’t know that I’d say I feel detached from people. I mean, I’ve been more caught up in my own head at times, but I haven’t really noticed losing interest in things in a clear way.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of the traumatic event?

Yes. I avoid the inspection bay if I can. I’ll take a longer way around just so I don’t have to pass it. And I don’t really talk about the accident unless I absolutely have to. I also stopped going to those industrial-history talks I used to like, because when they show pictures of old machinery, it sets me off.
Have you noticed yourself having negative thoughts about yourself, other people, or the world, like 'I’m bad,' 'people can’t be trusted,' or 'the world is completely dangerous'?

Yes. I don’t trust that plant anymore, or the people in charge of it. I keep thinking they let things get unsafe, and now I don’t know what to believe from them. And some days I look at myself and think I’m damaged goods… like I can’t even do the job I spent my whole life getting good at.
